newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian praline maker goes to bourse after 140 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian praline maker goes to bourse after 140 yrs.

text.p: Belgian luxury chocolate maker Neuhaus NV said on Wednesday it would seek a bourse listing for the first time in its 140 year history.
Guy Ullens de Schooten, chief executive officer of parent company Artal Nederland BV, said Neuhaus had arrived at the right stage in its development for a listing.
From one shop in in the centre of Brussels, Neuhaus -- which invented pralines in 1912 -- has grown into a worldwide business with sales in 36 countries.
Its own stores, franchises and outlets in retailers such as Harrods, Karstadt, Macy's and Galeries Lafayette achieve annual turnover in excess of 1.5 billion Belgian francs ($43 million).

Starting February 20, Artal is offering 450,000 Neuhaus shares to institutional and private investors at a price of between 1,600 and 1,750 Belgian francs (around $48) each. It has also applied to have all 750,000 Neuhaus shares listed on the Brussels Stock Exchange from March 10.
"Neuhaus has become a solid, stable growing company," said Pierre le Beau of lead managers Petercam, a Belgian brokerage.

Petercam forecast net earnings for the year ending June 30, 1997 of 61 million Belgian francs, up from 35 million in the year-earlier period. Gross current earnings should grow at around 24 percent a year until 2001, it added.
Neuhaus chief executive officer Marlene Vonken said Neuhaus's existing production units had ample room to expand capacity, but it was also looking for external growth.
"We will make acquisitions that complement our product lines and our distribution channels," she said.

Neuhaus presently has four businesses. Three praline units: Neuhaus and Jeff de Bruges, which respectively accounted for 47 percent and 35 percent of 1995/96 sales, and Mondose; and Union, which makes chocolates for use as corporate gifts or souvenirs.

Seventy two percent of the group's turnover is realised in Belgium and France. Vonken said, however, Germany, which at the moment accounts for seven percent of sales, should become its "second home market."
By seeking a listing, Neuhaus will join a select handful of quoted choclate makers, including British Thorntons and Austrian Josef Manner & Co.
